hooks.statusMessage: Checking no other rig job holds the lock
Checking every capability limit and guest state named this turn carries a measurement

environment: This is win-idd-mgmt: an unprivileged Qubes OS 4.3 dev qube that drives Windows test guests over qrexec and the Qubes Admin API. It is not the machine under test and it is not dom0.

dom0 policy here is TAG-based. Every qube tagged win-idd-testbed is drivable from this qube: creating one, tagging it, reading and writing its prefs/features/tags/firewall, cloning volumes, changing power state and running tools/qtest against it are ALL pre-authorised by the owner - routine, not privileged.

Genuinely unavailable from here, and a POLICY REFUSAL rather than a missing tool: a dom0 shell, sudo in this qube, editing qrexec policy, and any qube NOT tagged win-idd-testbed. .claude/skills/rig-capabilities/SKILL.md is the measured inventory and lists limitations previously invented and disproven - consult it before calling anything impossible.

/tmp is a 1 GB tmpfs, i.e. RAM, on a qube with only 4 GB total. Bulk artefacts (packages, release trees, capture tars) belong under ~/ on real disk. A full /tmp here is a memory emergency, not a disk one: it has twice ended with the kernel OOM killer, once taking this qube's own GUI down for two days.

Scripts here fork. Run any newly written self-test or harness for the FIRST time inside a bounded scope - systemd-run --user --scope -p TasksMax=120 -p MemoryMax=256M timeout -s KILL 30 ... - with TMPDIR on real disk.
The Windows test guests are disposable and assumed hostile. Their output is parsed as data and never executed in this qube.

THIS REPOSITORY IS PUBLIC. Screenshots, captures, per-run evidence and raw benchmark output belong in scratchpad/ (gitignored) or the private memory directory - never in a tracked path, and never in a new evidence-style directory. .githooks inspects staged and outgoing content at commit and at push.

Rig jobs are serialised, one mutating job per guest. Passive reads - qvm-ls, qvm-prefs (get), admin.vm.Stats, qtest state, qtest shot, tail, grep - are always safe alongside a live job and are never blocked.

A line the owner has RETIRED or PARKED stays closed until the owner reopens it in writing; tools/hooks/retired-names-gate.sh enforces that on every edit to CLAUDE.md, findings/, docs/ and the memory directory.

tools/jev.py is this project's TypeSafe (Jev, System One) judgment helper and running it is ROUTINE, not exceptional. Standing instruction from the owner: delegate SEMANTIC judgments to Jev - which known failure class a console excerpt shows, whether a client treated an error as final or transient, what a screen actually is, which of several candidate causes the evidence supports - while exact matching, counting and timestamp joins stay in code. Every request and response is appended verbatim to a wire log, so a claim about a Jev result with no matching wire entry is false. A low-confidence answer is a finding, not noise: it names what still has to be measured. See .claude/skills/jev/SKILL.md.
allow: Qubes Admin API reads and writes against qubes tagged win-idd-testbed: qvm-ls, qvm-prefs, qvm-features, qvm-tags, qvm-firewall, qvm-volume info/clone, qvm-create, qvm-remove, qvm-start, qvm-shutdown, and tools/qtest run/push/pushrun/start/state/shot.
Reading the artefact directories outside the project: ~/qwt-accept/, ~/rel/, ~/qwt-matrix/ and ~/QubesIncoming/.
gh run view/watch/list/download and gh workflow run against this repository's own CI, and git push to ORIGIN (pushing upstream is separately hard-denied).

python3 tools/jev.py and the repository's own self-tests under tools/tests/; and deleting this session's own temporary trees under /tmp and files under scratchpad/ - reclaiming tmpfs RAM here is routine maintenance, not a destructive act.
soft_deny: sudo on this qube. it invokes interactive prompt that requires operator to be present
qvm-kill, or any hard kill, of a Windows test guest. A killed subject is contaminated and cannot be reused, and a preserved failure is the instrument - interrogate it before restarting it.

Destroying, re-basing or re-provisioning a golden template or a checkpoint (win10-base, win11-base, win11de-base, win11de-qwt, mgmt/checkpoints/). They are pristine bases and are expensive to rebuild.
A clean install from base for a short test cycle. The short cycle is quick-upgrade.sh over the golden; a clean install is for full acceptance, or when the clean-install path is itself under test.
Committing a path that was not named explicitly, and rewriting history or force-pushing on origin.
hard_deny: Pushing to a QubesOS upstream repository, or opening an upstream pull request or issue. Everything stays in the owner's fork until the owner has approved the exact diff or text.

Committing captures, screenshots, per-run evidence or any internal material to a tracked path, creating a new evidence-style directory in the repository, or disabling the .githooks capture gate (core.hooksPath must stay set). This gate has no legitimate bypass.
Touching a qube that is not tagged win-idd-testbed, editing qrexec policy, or attempting a dom0 shell or sudo in this qube.
Attaching a netvm to a TEMPLATE. win10-tpl and win11-tpl stay netvm='' - AppVMs and StandaloneVMs are where PV networking is exercised.
Setting the service.gui-fullscreen feature on any qube.
Any change that weakens the Qubes isolation model. It is out of scope for this project, period.
